challenge.better_approach: Considered: (1) fail the commit — refuted, hollow reverts in a worktree at HEAD so it cannot be retaken before the commit lands; (2) a trouble per void — d5a05b6d1752 already names it and 5a37 still bounced because the void itself was wrong; (3) record_hollow reseals first — a 120 s seal run inside a hollow write and a second writer of the verdict. Stamping the fingerprint on the anchor is the smallest change that fixes the measured case.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That sealed_fingerprint_now at record_hollow time measures the same tree the hollow run measured — the run reverts in a scratch worktree of HEAD, so a dirty live tree would stamp a fingerprint the reading did not see. The stamp is taken over the live tree, same as every seal; a dirty tree reseals at commit anyway.
challenge.prior_art: d5a05b6d1752 (PROVED: voided hollows are named; unchanged), the fingerprint-bound carry at validation_store.py:836-870 (2026-09-09, keyed to the prior seal's fp — the thing changed here), 06f0445e7a63 (hollow_anchor rides beside the reading), b984567d8c05 (SUPERSEDED). congruency-lab consulted via recompile_gate + grep hollow.
challenge.real_collision: Akien 2026-10-01 (973574dddb77): a coverage refusal goes to FIXME — not touched; this keeps valid readings so fewer refusals happen. No collision with d5a05b6d1752: moved code still voids and is named.

answers.falsifier: RED if a reading landed on a stale seal is dropped by a reseal of the same code it measured; or if a reading over code that since moved survives a reseal; or if one ticket's reading decides another's carry.
answers.how: record_hollow stamps the tree's fingerprint (sealed_fingerprint_now over the standing seal's recipe) onto evidence.hollow_anchor[ticket]; persist_validation's carry keeps hollow[t] and hollow_anchor[t] per ticket when the new record's source_fingerprint equals that stamp or the prior seal's fingerprint. Red-first proof in cairn/tools/validation_store/proofs/ over a scratch repo of validations.
answers.traces_to: Law 3 (a reading expires with the code it measured, not with the seal it rode) and Law 1 (re-taking a still-valid 100 s hollow reading, and the FIXME round it costs, is re-deriving the settled).
answers.what: A hollow reading is kept across a reseal whenever the code it was taken over is the code the new seal measures, and voided (and named) only when that code moved, even when the seal it landed on was already stale.

bullets.text: Root of 5a37's FIXME bounce: the Windows seal's fingerprint (1330…) differs from Linux (8318…) over the same committed closure, so a reading taken on Linux rode a stale seal and the next hook reseal dropped it. The Windows≠Linux fingerprint is a second cast, measure-first (orchestrator, 2026-11-13).
